title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat, made with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat is a dish made from beaten eggs cooked in vegetable oil with added pieces of cooked or fried meat (commonly ham, sausage or bacon). The eggs provide high‑quality protein, while the meat adds extra iron and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is popular in many cuisines, from the American breakfast plate to Russian fried eggs with sausage.
Cooking in oil gives the omelet a crisp edge and enhances the flavor of the meat.
Combining eggs and meat creates a more satiating meal than either ingredient alone.
In Soviet-era cooking the closest analogue is “fried eggs with sausage,” often served in school cafeterias.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs and meat together provide a complete set of essential amino acids that support tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat, especially beef and poultry, supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both eggs and meat are good sources of B12, B6 and niacin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: The vegetable oil (e.g., sunflower or canola) contributes polyunsaturated fatty acids needed for cell‑membrane health.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and fat slows gastric emptying, helping to control appetite.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The dish contains a notable amount of fat and calories, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Cholesterol
items.content: Eggs are high in cholesterol; individuals with elevated cholesterol levels should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs may harbor Salmonella, and insufficiently cooked meat can contain harmful bacteria. Cook until fully set.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Heat oil in a skillet, add diced meat and fry until golden. Pour the egg mixture over the meat, stirring gently until the eggs are set but still tender. Serve hot, optionally garnished with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The dish is best enjoyed immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours and reheat before serving.
